name: GRE General Test
description: Graduate Record Examination testing Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning, and Analytical Writing.

difficulty_scale.label: Easy
difficulty_scale.definition: Simple recall, basic calculations, or direct reading checks.

difficulty_scale.label: Medium
difficulty_scale.definition: Intermediate problem solving, simple double blank context, or multi-step math.

difficulty_scale.label: Hard
difficulty_scale.definition: Calibrated to the hardest ~10% of REAL GRE Quant questions — NOT competition/olympiad math. Requires synthesizing 2-3 standard skills (algebra, arithmetic, basic geometry/stats — no calculus, no obscure theorems), a non-obvious first step, or resolving deliberately close distractors, while remaining solvable in roughly 90-120 seconds with clean numbers. Difficulty comes from reasoning/insight, not from computational grind or content outside the standard GRE curriculum.

style_rules: Text Completion must have exactly 5 options for single blanks, or distinct options per blank.
Quantitative Comparison must present two quantities (Quantity A and Quantity B) and require comparing them.
Sentence Equivalence must require choosing EXACTLY TWO options that lead to equivalent and coherent sentence meanings.

checks.description: Is the solution key or essay rubric completely verified?
Do distractors represent advanced logical fallacies or sophisticated math trap answers?
Is the prompt free of ambiguity and grammatically pristine?
Is the difficulty calibrated to the graduate school standard?
Does the question map directly to GRE competencies?
Is the content completely original and uncopied?
Is it fair to international graduate school applicants?
